summary: Starlane Chat: out-of-order completions across multiplexed shards causing inconsistent conversation state and urgent customer escalation
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 01:15 UTC and 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC Starlane observed a sequence of chat completions delivered out-of-order for multi-turn conversations. The customer first reported cases where assistant replies for later user messages appeared before earlier replies, causing application state divergence and automated downstream actions triggering on incorrect prompts. Immediate impact: service interruptions for live chat flows, customer escalated to enterprise support and threatened failover to alternative provider.
impact: Multiple customer production chat sessions returned out-of-order transcript chunks. Approx. 8% of requests from Starlane routed through their dedicated shard pool experienced ordering inversion. Several automated downstream actions (message routing, billing triggers) were executed incorrectly. Business impact included degraded UX and potential downstream transaction mismatches.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Starlane's multi-turn chat client configured with streaming=true and multiplexing across 4 shards.
2) Send sequences of short-turn user messages spaced <200ms apart to trigger concurrent KV cache use and multiplexed requests.
3) Observe that later completions arrive before earlier ones in ~1 in 12 trials under the failure window conditions.
4) Reproduced on redwood-chat-3b and quantized variant when kernel-selector chosen 'fast-kv-opt-v2' under burst load.
logs: 2026-03-10T01:19:01Z serving-runtime.ERROR request_id=def456 kvcache: stale-prefix-detected; falling back to full-loading
Trace snippets and session IDs provided to customer via secure attachment and internal S3 logs (link in related_confluence_pages).
comments: 2026-03-10 01:40 - Support (Priya): A customer (Starlane) reported out-of-order streaming completions. They've opened a high-priority escalation and asked for immediate mitigation. Logged initial traces and requested a conference bridge.

2026-03-10 01:52 - SRE (Ethan): Identified pattern where multiplexed shard responses become non-deterministic when 'fast-kv-opt-v2' kernel selection coincides with concurrent prefix cache refresh. Hypothesis: race between sequencer ack and multiplexer flush path.

2026-03-10 02:08 - Eng (Miguel): Pushed temporary sequencer change to enforce per-session monotonic ordering: single-flight sequencer lock for sessions on Starlane's pool. Rolling restart to pool applied at 02:12 UTC.

2026-03-10 02:25 - Support (Priya): Customer verified vast majority of impacted sessions now show correct ordering; they still report intermittent edge cases on heavy bursts. Customer requested rollback of 'fast-kv-opt-v2' kernel selection for their pool while we investigate.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Eng (Ethan): Deployed hotfix to multiplexer flush ordering and added stricter idempotency checks; kernel selection override scheduled for Starlane pool (downgrade to 'kv-stable-v1') at 2026-03-11 10:30 UTC. Monitoring shows no further reorders for 24h.
2026-03-12 14:10 - Support (Priya): Customer acknowledged remediation and accepted rollback and monitoring. Incident marked Resolved. Agreed to follow-up actions and credit discussion.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: race between KV cache refresh and multiplexer flush where response order metadata was lost when a shard's response buffer was force-flushed during prefix reload.
Confirmed via trace correlation: request_id groups showed non-monotonic 'sent_seq' timestamps with overlapping flush windows on the same consumer socket.

Root cause: two factors combined - a) an aggressive kernel variant ('fast-kv-opt-v2') that triggers a micro-batching optimization producing out-of-order responses when NVMe-backed KV loads spike, and b) the multiplexer did not reattach per-session sequence fences after a fast-path cache refill.
resolution: Applied emergency mitigations: 1) Temporarily enforced per-session sequencer lock for Starlane's dedicated shard pool to guarantee ordering; 2) Overrode kernel selection for their pool to 'kv-stable-v1' to avoid micro-batching path; 3) Deployed a targeted hotfix to multiplexer ordering (idempotency checks and fence reattachment). Verified with customer traffic and internal load tests. No further out-of-order deliveries observed after 24h monitoring window. Customer provided credits for incident impact and accepted proposed post-incident plan.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering to ship a full multiplexer ordering regression test (automated) to CI by 2026-03-20.
2) Runtime team to audit kernel selection heuristics and add a safety gate that avoids 'fast-kv-opt-v2' for any pool with high concurrency and short-turn latencies by 2026-03-18.
3) SRE to add a session-sequence monotonicity alert to paging rules (pager threshold: >0.5% reorders over 5m) by 2026-03-15.
4) CS to provide customer-facing postmortem and credit details; schedule review with Starlane on 2026-03-18.
5) Product to evaluate adding a per-customer kernel pin feature in Console to avoid unexpected kernel transitions during bursts (design review 2026-04-01).
notes_for_billing: Customer impacted sessions estimated ~1.2k failed-order events; support recommended 20% service credit for affected window. Finance ticket to reconcile credit scheduled.
post_incident_summary: Starlane experienced an out-of-order completion bug stemming from the interaction between an aggressive kernel optimization and the multiplexer flush path under bursty, short-turn loads. Immediate mitigations removed the optimizer from their pool and enforced sequencing locks; a hotfix to multiplexer ordering removed the root cause. Follow-ups include regression tests, alerting, kernel-selection safety gates, and a potential Console feature to pin kernels per-customer.
customer_communication: Provided status updates during the incident via private Slack (#support-starlane) and daily wrap-up emails. A scheduled call on 2026-03-12 covered technical findings, mitigation steps, and proposed credits. Customer accepted fixes and will participate in follow-up postmortem.
resolution_notes: Incident declared Resolved 2026-03-12 after 48 hours of zero reorders in production for Starlane pool. Hotfix merged and cherry-picked to release branch. Postmortem meeting scheduled for 2026-03-18.
